title: Medicaid in Minnesota: Fraudsters owe millions but pay back little
jurisdiction: Minnesota state courts; U.S. District Court (District of Minnesota) referenced for federal-tool comparison
notes: Independent FOX 9 investigative analysis, published roughly 11 weeks before the KSTP 2026-08-03 analysis and covering a narrower, differently-scoped case set. Do not merge its totals with the KSTP figures in src-kstp-2026-08-03-restitution-collection-analysis; see contradiction-restitution-collection-scope-kstp-vs-fox9.
supports: FOX 9 identified 48 Minnesota Medicaid fraud cases since 2020 with a combined $13.3 million in restitution ordered.
As of spring 2026, approximately $2.355 million (about 17.7%) of that $13.3 million had been repaid, leaving roughly $11 million outstanding.
Individual case restitution amounts in the reviewed set ranged from $69 to $1.7 million.
Defendant Ali Ismail Warsame was reported to owe $667,719 in restitution.
Defendant Xiaoyan Hu was ordered to pay restitution of more than $500,000; more than $284,000 was reported recovered from Hu's accounts.
A pending asset-seizure action in a separate case was reported at $650,000.
One case's restitution order, reported at $21,590, was tied to a case that was later dismissed.

Attorney General Keith Ellison acknowledged the federal government has tools (such as asset seizure) that Minnesota state prosecutors reportedly lack, and noted Minnesota probation terms can end before restitution is fully paid.

system_metrics.notes: Scope is FOX 9's own reviewed set of 48 cases, not stated to be all MFCU-prosecuted cases since 2019/2020.
~17.7% collection rate against the $13.3M figure for this specific 48-case set.

does_not_support: That the 48-case, $13.3M/2020-forward set is the same population as KSTP's 2019-forward, $32M MFCU-wide figure; the case counts, start years, and totals differ and the source does not reconcile them.
A full accounting of every MFCU restitution case; this is a reviewed sample, not stated to be exhaustive.
